---
title: Quick start
description: Detect basic anomalies in a synthetic water-level time series
jupyter: tsod
---

This example shows a minimal end-to-end workflow on water-level data.

## Imports

```{python}
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

from tsod import RangeDetector
```

## Create sample data

```{python}
rng = np.random.default_rng(42)
time = pd.date_range("2025-01-01", periods=240, freq="h")

baseline = 1.5 + 0.2 * np.sin(np.linspace(0, 6 * np.pi, len(time)))
noise = rng.normal(0, 0.03, len(time))
water_level = baseline + noise

# Inject a few unrealistic spikes
water_level[[40, 120, 180]] = [2.4, 0.2, 2.6]

series = pd.Series(water_level, index=time, name="water_level_m")
series.head()
```

## Detect anomalies

```{python}
detector = RangeDetector(min_value=0.8, max_value=2.1)
anomalies = detector.detect(series)

anomalies.sum()
```

## Visualize results

```{python}
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(10, 4))
series.plot(ax=ax, label="Water level")
series[anomalies].plot(ax=ax, linestyle="", marker="o", color="red", label="Anomaly")
ax.set_ylabel("m")
ax.set_title("Quick anomaly screening")
ax.legend()
```
